question: How do fitted repeat-aware versus naive learner-state encoders affect finite-data Q-learning exercise selection under transfer, repair-only and misspecified learning dynamics?
data_scope: Entirely synthetic students and six virtual tasks; no human records and no mapping to RetryLab Python exercises.
claim_scope: Software validation and descriptive policy performance conditional on declared simulators; no SOTA, human learning efficacy, or validated app integration.
primary_metric: Mean final minus initial expected success on three independent unpractised skill probes; compare q_repeat_aware with q_naive separately in each world.

split.evaluation_seeds: 900000000 + world_index*1000000 + episode; same across policies and fitted seeds for paired comparison
split.worlds: Train only transfer_and_repair; evaluate that world plus zero learning, slow learning, stronger forgetting and structurally different prerequisite coupling. All mechanisms specified before first evaluation.

selection: Learner parameters minimize training NLL on a fixed grid; validation NLL is descriptive only. Fixed Q-learning budget/configuration, no checkpoint selection or tuning on evaluation outcomes. Report all policies/worlds/seeds, including null or unfavorable results.
learner_model: Approximate BKT-style filter over 3 skills. Grid learn=[.04,.1,.16], guess=[.15,.25], slip=[.08,.16], memory=[0] naive or [0,.35,.65] repeat-aware. Prior .3 and forgetting .005 assumed. All observations precede their updates.
policy: Tabular Q-learning, alpha=.15, gamma=1, linear epsilon .3 to .05. State: remaining horizon, 3-bin beliefs and capped per-skill attempt counts. Actions: six virtual exercises, each at most twice. Partial observation/coarse state means this is an approximate state representation, not an established sufficient Markov state.
reward: Per-step -.005 * simulated action time cost; terminal observed independent probe fraction. No latent mastery in policy inputs or rewards. Evaluation additionally accesses simulator latent mastery to compute expected probe gain without item-familiarity credit.
fallback: Unseen Q states use estimated weakest-skill rule; report fallback fraction for the resulting hybrid policy.
uncertainty: Descriptive per-seed results and min/max across 3 fits, with paired mean differences. No confidence interval or significance claim. Shared evaluation learners across fits are not independent replicates.
limitations: Hand-specified educational mechanisms and virtual tasks
Small fixed parameter grid and coarse observation state
No proven novelty or venue readiness
